title: A note on Coulomb collision operator in curvilinear coordinates
central_proposition: The paper generalizes the expressions for the dynamic friction force and diffusion tensor in velocity space, and the Coulomb collision term, to curvilinear coordinates using both partial (Trubnikov) and summed (Rosenbluth) potential functions in plasma physics.

concept_definitions.name: Coulomb collision operator
concept_definitions.definition: A term in the kinetic equation describing the effect of Coulomb interactions (collisions) between charged particles in a plasma.

concept_definitions.name: Dynamic friction force
concept_definitions.definition: A component of the force acting on test particles due to collisions with background plasma particles, expressed as minus the gradient of a scalar potential in velocity space.

concept_definitions.name: Diffusion tensor
concept_definitions.definition: A tensor describing the diffusion of test particles in velocity space due to collisions, expressed as a Hessian tensor associated with a scalar potential.

concept_definitions.name: Flux density in velocity space
concept_definitions.definition: The rate at which particles move through velocity space due to collisions, composed of dynamic friction and diffusion terms.

concept_definitions.name: Trubnikov potential functions
concept_definitions.definition: Partial scalar (Φ_αβ) and vector (Ψ_αβ) potential functions defined for each species of background plasma, used to express collision terms.

concept_definitions.name: Rosenbluth potential functions
concept_definitions.definition: Potential functions (H_α and G_α) summed over all species of background plasma, also used to express collision terms.

concept_definitions.name: Curvilinear coordinates
concept_definitions.definition: A coordinate system where coordinate lines are curved, allowing for more general geometric descriptions than Cartesian coordinates.

argument_structure: The paper first reproduces equivalent formulations of the Coulomb collision term in Cartesian coordinates using both Trubnikov and Rosenbluth potential functions. It then generalizes these expressions for the dynamic friction force, diffusion tensor, and collision term to arbitrary curvilinear coordinates by replacing partial derivatives with covariant derivatives and incorporating metric tensors and Christoffel symbols.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The mechanism involves expressing the dynamic friction force as a covariant gradient of a scalar potential and the diffusion tensor as a covariant Hessian tensor of another scalar potential. The collision term is then derived as the negative covariant divergence of the collisional flux density in velocity space, which itself is a function of these forces and tensors. This generalization ensures the mathematical consistency of the collision operator in non-Cartesian coordinate systems.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic friction force in Cartesian coordinates
findings.consequent: Minus gradient of the modified scalar potential Φ_αβ
findings.mechanism: Defined as the negative gradient of the potential function Φ_αβ in velocity space, representing the force experienced by test particles due to collisions.

findings.consequent: Hessian tensor associated with the modified scalar potential Ψ_αβ
findings.mechanism: Defined as the second partial derivative of the potential function Ψ_αβ with respect to velocity components, describing the spread of particles in velocity space.

findings.antecedent: Partial flux density of particles α in velocity space due to collisions with particles β in Cartesian coordinates
findings.consequent: Sum of dynamic friction term and diffusion term
findings.mechanism: Composed of a dynamic friction term (proportional to F^i_αβ) and a diffusion term (proportional to D^ij_αβ), representing the net flow of particles in velocity space.
findings.quote: γ^i_αβ = F^i_αβ (n_α f_α) / m_α - D^ij_αβ ∂(n_α f_α) / ∂v^j

findings.consequent: Minus divergence of the partial flux density γ^i_αβ
findings.mechanism: The collision term, representing the rate of change of the distribution function due to collisions, is defined as the negative divergence of the flux density in velocity space, ensuring particle conservation.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic friction force in curvilinear coordinates
findings.consequent: Contravariant coordinates F^i expressed as g^ik ∂Φ_αβ/∂v^k
findings.mechanism: Generalization of the Cartesian gradient to curvilinear coordinates using the contravariant metric tensor g^ik to transform the covariant gradient into contravariant components.

findings.consequent: Covariant Hessian tensor D_ij expressed as ∂²Ψ_αβ/∂v^i∂v^j - Γ^k_ij ∂Ψ_αβ/∂v^k
findings.mechanism: Generalization of the Cartesian Hessian to curvilinear coordinates by replacing partial derivatives with covariant derivatives, involving Christoffel symbols Γ^k_ij to account for the curvature of the coordinate system.

findings.antecedent: Partial flux density γ^i_αβ in curvilinear coordinates
findings.consequent: Contravariant coordinates expressed via F^i_αβ and D_jk with metric tensor g^kl
findings.mechanism: The flux density is formulated using the contravariant components of the dynamic friction force and the diffusion tensor, adapted for curvilinear coordinates.
findings.quote: γ^i_αβ = F^i_αβ (n_α f_α) / m_α - g^ik D_jk g^jl ∂(n_α f_α) / ∂v^l

findings.antecedent: Partial collision term C_αβ in curvilinear coordinates
findings.consequent: Negative covariant divergence of the partial flux density γ^i_αβ
findings.mechanism: The collision term is expressed as the negative covariant divergence of the flux density, which is the appropriate generalization of the divergence operator in curvilinear coordinates.

findings.antecedent: Full dynamic friction force F^i in curvilinear coordinates (Rosenbluth potentials)
findings.consequent: Contravariant components expressed via H_α potential and metric tensor
findings.mechanism: Derived from the H_α potential, generalized to curvilinear coordinates using covariant derivatives and metric tensors, representing the total friction force from all background species.

findings.antecedent: Full diffusion tensor D_mk in curvilinear coordinates (Rosenbluth potentials)
findings.consequent: Covariant components expressed via G_α potential and Christoffel symbols
findings.mechanism: Derived from the G_α potential, generalized to curvilinear coordinates using covariant derivatives and Christoffel symbols, representing the total diffusion from all background species.

findings.antecedent: Full collision term C_α in curvilinear coordinates
findings.consequent: Negative covariant divergence of the full flux density γ^i_α
findings.mechanism: The total collision term is expressed as the negative covariant divergence of the total flux density, consistent with the generalization for partial collision terms.

model_structure: The paper presents a mathematical model for the Coulomb collision operator, extending its formulation from Cartesian to general curvilinear coordinates. The model defines dynamic friction force and diffusion tensor using scalar potential functions (Trubnikov or Rosenbluth potentials) and then combines these into a collisional flux density. The collision term itself is defined as the negative divergence of this flux density. The core structure involves replacing standard partial derivatives with covariant derivatives and incorporating the metric tensor and Christoffel symbols to account for the geometry of the curvilinear coordinate system.
limitations: This paper is a theoretical derivation in plasma physics and does not address the built environment, human cognition, emotion, behavior, or health. Its findings are mathematical formulas for physical phenomena in plasma, not psychological or environmental responses.
